quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #24
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: When are streets and highways most slippery?

options.text: When it has been raining hard for several hours.
When they are clean and dry.
Just after it starts to rain.

questions.correctAnswerText: Just after it starts to rain.
questions.explanation: Roads are most slippery when rain first starts. Water mixes with oil and dirt on the road surface that has not yet washed away. Drive with extra caution in the first half hour of rain.

questions.question: To avoid traffic merging from on-ramps on an interstate, what should you do?

options.text: Change lanes to the left.
Slow down.
Maintain your speed and position.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes to the left.
questions.explanation: When you see an on-ramp ahead, move to the left lane when it is safe. This lets vehicles enter the freeway from the right side.

questions.question: A large truck is turning right onto a street with two lanes in each direction. What may happen?

options.text: May complete its turn in either of the two lanes.
May have to swing wide to complete the right turn.
Must stay in the right lane at all times while turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: May have to swing wide to complete the right turn.
questions.explanation: Long trucks need more space to turn. The rear wheels follow a shorter path than the front wheels, so trucks often swing wide to complete a right turn.

questions.question: Having a driver license is a:

options.text: Requirement.
Privilege.
Right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Privilege.
questions.explanation: Driving is a privilege, not a right. All drivers must drive safely. If you abuse this privilege, it can be taken away.

questions.question: If your tires lose contact with the road, what should you do?

options.text: Slow down by shifting into a lower gear.
Ease your foot off the gas pedal.
Slow down by pumping the brakes quickly and firmly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ease your foot off the gas pedal.
questions.explanation: If your tires lose grip, ease off the gas and stay off the brakes. Do not try to stop or turn until your tires grip the road again.

questions.question: If you don't see a gap in traffic when entering the freeway, what should you do?

options.text: Maintain your speed and force the other drivers to create a gap.
Slow down on the ramp to wait for a gap.
Stop at the end of the ramp to wait for a gap.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down on the ramp to wait for a gap.
questions.explanation: Slow down on the ramp if you don't see a safe opening. Do not stop at the end of the ramp, as you won't have enough room to speed up before entering the freeway.

questions.question: How can you avoid hydroplaning while driving in rain?

options.text: Drive at a speed appropriate for ideal conditions.
Apply your brakes as soon as your car starts to skid.
Slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when tires lose contact with the wet road. To prevent it, drive slower in rain than you would in dry conditions.

questions.question: On a green arrow, you must:

options.text: Yield to any vehicle, bicycle, or pedestrian in the intersection.
Yield to pedestrians only in the intersection.
Wait four seconds before proceeding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to any vehicle, bicycle, or pedestrian in the intersection.
questions.explanation: A green arrow means you can turn. First, yield to any vehicles, bicycles, or pedestrians still in the intersection, then turn in the direction the arrow points.

questions.question: Which road is most likely to be slippery in cold weather after snow or rain?

options.text: A hilly, open road
A residential road
A road in a shaded area

questions.correctAnswerText: A road in a shaded area
questions.explanation: Shaded areas freeze before the rest of the road and thaw out later. In cold, wet weather, these spots become icy and slippery.

questions.question: Alcohol is:

options.text: A stimulant.
An antihistamine.
A depressant.

questions.correctAnswerText: A depressant.
questions.explanation: Alcohol is a depressant. It slows your thinking and makes your reflexes unreliable.

questions.question: When parking on a hill, what should you do?

options.text: One of your rear wheels should touch the curb.
Use your parking brake and leave the vehicle in "park."
Your front wheels should be parallel to the road, if there is no curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your parking brake and leave the vehicle in "park."
questions.explanation: Always use your parking brake and put the car in "park." If there is no curb, turn your front wheels away from the road center. If there is a curb, turn toward it when heading downhill or away from it when heading uphill.

questions.question: When entering a freeway, how should you check traffic?

options.text: Using your rearview and side mirrors.
Using your rearview mirror.
Using your side mirror and looking over your shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Using your side mirror and looking over your shoulder.
questions.explanation: Use your side mirror and look over your shoulder to see traffic when entering the freeway. This helps you see and plan for traffic safely.

questions.question: When you see a flashing red light at an intersection, you must:

options.text: Come to a complete stop, yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians, then proceed.
Reduce your speed and proceed with caution.
Come to a complete stop and remain stopped as long as the light is red.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop, yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians, then proceed.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light works like a stop sign. Stop completely. Then proceed when it is safe and you have yielded to all traffic and pedestrians.

questions.question: Why should you not use high beam headlights in fog or mist?

options.text: The light reflects back into your eyes.
Oncoming vehicles cannot see you.
Vehicles behind you may follow too closely.

questions.correctAnswerText: The light reflects back into your eyes.
questions.explanation: In fog or mist, high beam headlights reflect back into your eyes. Use low beams instead.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Railroad crossing ahead.
No passing zone.
School zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Railroad crossing ahead.
questions.explanation: A round yellow sign with black markings warns that a railroad crossing is ahead.

questions.question: When changing lanes, what should you never do?

options.text: Change lanes while inside an intersection.
Check your blind spot by looking over your shoulder.
Check for other drivers moving into the same lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes while inside an intersection.
questions.explanation: Never change lanes while inside an intersection. Always check your blind spot over your shoulder. Always watch for other drivers who may be moving into the same lane.

questions.question: If a tire suddenly blows out, what should you do?

options.text: Use the brakes lightly.
Pump the brakes.
Apply the brakes hard.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the brakes lightly.
questions.explanation: If a tire blows out, hold the steering wheel firmly and keep the vehicle straight. Slow down by releasing the gas pedal and applying the brakes gently.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Pedestrians walking along the road ahead.
Pedestrian crossing ahead.
Pedestrians cannot cross here.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pedestrian crossing ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. This sign warns drivers that pedestrians may be crossing. Stop and remain stopped until the pedestrian has completely crossed.

questions.question: What should you do when driving at night?

options.text: Always use high beam headlights.
Look directly at oncoming headlights.
Keep a greater distance between you and the vehicle ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep a greater distance between you and the vehicle ahead.
questions.explanation: Night driving is more dangerous because visibility is lower. Increase the distance between your vehicle and the one ahead. This gives you more time to stop if the front vehicle stops suddenly.

questions.question: Why should you increase your following distance behind a large vehicle?

options.text: To see better around the sides of the vehicle.
Because drivers tend to pass large vehicles from behind.
Because the vehicle's slipstream will pull you forward if you follow too closely.

questions.correctAnswerText: To see better around the sides of the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Truck, bus, and van drivers may not see you if you drive directly behind them. Keep more distance so you can see around the vehicle and see the road ahead.

questions.question: When must Arkansas drivers turn on their headlights?

options.text: When driving closely behind another vehicle.
When windshield wipers are in use.
When they want to get someone's attention.

questions.correctAnswerText: When windshield wipers are in use.
questions.explanation: Arkansas law requires headlights to be on when windshield wipers are needed. Use low beams in rain, snow, and fog.

questions.question: What should you do at a flashing red traffic light?

options.text: You are traveling the wrong direction.
Treat it like a stop sign.
You cannot go until it turns green.

questions.correctAnswerText: Treat it like a stop sign.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means stop. Come to a complete stop at the stop line or before the crosswalk. Yield to all traffic and pedestrians before proceeding.

questions.question: What does this sign tell you about the road ahead?

options.text: It turns sharply right, then left.
It curves right, then left.
It curves right.

questions.correctAnswerText: It curves right, then left.
questions.explanation: This sign warns drivers that the road curves right and then curves left.

questions.question: When can your license be suspended for driving under 21 with alcohol in your system?

options.text: At 0.15 percent or more.
At 0.08 percent or more.
At any amount.

questions.correctAnswerText: At any amount.
questions.explanation: There is zero tolerance for alcohol if you are under 21. Any trace of alcohol will result in serious penalties, including a two-year license suspension.

questions.question: When changing lanes, what should you never do?

options.text: Cross the centerline in an intersection.
Check your blind spots by looking over your shoulder.
Check for other drivers moving into the same lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cross the centerline in an intersection.
questions.explanation: Never pass or change lanes in an intersection. Always check your blind spot by looking over your shoulder. Watch for other drivers who may be entering the same lane.
